correctness.rationale: On \(A=I_2\) with two independent uniform reflections, the product is exactly \(\pm I_2\) with equal probabilities. Conditional expectation of the exact fixed-momentum recurrence yields the displayed three-state moment matrix with no approximation. At zero momentum its simple eigenvalue is \(s\); the left/right eigenvector derivative gives \(2\alpha(1-\alpha)(2\alpha-1)/s\). The source initial moment vector excites this branch. At \(\alpha=1/2\) the cubic gives the positive second-order coefficient. The rational witness is verified by three disjoint exact sign-change intervals for its degree-three characteristic polynomial and the exact source bound constants.

originality.rationale: The defining RrDR source proves a mean-square upper bound and explicitly observes that its certified factor worsens with momentum, but separately proves acceleration only for the norm of expected iterates. Direct full-text comparison found no evaluation of the actual two-reflection Bernoulli second-moment operator. The same authors’ later improved-sampling and adaptive-momentum paper changes the sampling distribution or update; broad minibatch heavy-ball theory also does not imply this exact fixed-momentum mean-square phase transition. The novelty is the exact underrelaxation sign boundary and certified in-regime strict mean-square acceleration, not the generic possibility of heavy-ball acceleration.
residual_risks: The moment matrix also describes a simple Bernoulli-stepsize heavy-ball model; an unindexed generic stochastic-recurrence note might state an equivalent local derivative under different terminology.

The acceleration is an asymptotic mean-square statement on the smallest full-rank orthonormal system; it does not claim practical dominance over alternative sampling policies or optimally tuned relaxation.
The defining paper’s upper-bound deterioration was never a claim that actual mean-square acceleration was impossible.

value.rationale: The defining algorithm’s main analysis explicitly separates mean-square guarantees from norm-of-mean acceleration and its own mean-square certificate suggests no momentum gain. The exact same source method, within the source theorem’s certified stability region, nevertheless improves the actual expected-squared-error rate under underrelaxation. The sharp transition at alpha one-half and rational parameter witness explain a mathematically meaningful gap between conservative guarantees and actual stochastic momentum dynamics; both compared runs use identical reflection budgets.
